author: Jason Paul Fox
title: The Quarry
bio:
Jason Paul Fox (1970-) was raised in Rochester, NY by a pack of wild lesbians. He was a child prodigy and attended Simon's Rock College, with a major in English, when he was only 15. In the beginning of the 1990's, he ran the almost very successful literary publication, Millenium Broadside (the second 'n' is missing on purpose and it was at a time when Y2K wasn't even a blip on society's collective radar) before a series of quick moves to and from Boston made his life too unstable to continue it.

He is a poet, graphic artist, musician, and philosopher. Jason is about as old-school in the Rochester artist's scene as you can get, having logged more party hours than a decrepted hard-lined communist and consuming just about as much vodka.

author: B. Edward Barrett
title: I: It's A Strange Invitation
serial_name: Panic and Revulsion in Washington D.C.
bio:
B. Edward Barrett was born in 1972 and lives in Rochester, NY. He was the editor of Cereal Magazine, a concert roadie, graphic artist, bohemic-living synchronisity guru and student at Monroe Community College where he studied Communication and Computer Science, and was the associate editor of Cabbages and Kings Literary Magazine. He is also a musician, photographer, a conspirator for the upcoming revolution and a connoisseur of fine coffee. Son of Norman and Sara, who met on the steps of the Capitol Building in Washington D.C. when they were a Navy photographer and FBI file clerk, named partially after a building nearby where the Grand Jury resides and raised in a Masonic Temple, Barrett has always felt a strange kinship to the D.C. area, politics and covert activity. http://brianebarrett.com/

Favorite authors include: Kurt Vonnegut Jr, Douglas Adams, Honore de Balzac, Guy de Maupausaunt, Ray Bradbury, Frederik Pohl, Shel Siverstein, Leo Tolstoy, William Gibson, William S. Burroughs, and Franz Kafka.

author: Garrett Kramer
title: The 13th Angry Viewer
bio: Garrett Kramer (aged 20) was the son of two loving parents, George and Deborah Kramer. Before his passing last July, Garrett was working on being carded in every bar in Rochester and getting slapped by every call girl in Syracuse. His goal would have been accomplished if not for John Stamos and his fitting revenge on his most vaunted critic. Garrett's last words were "the horror..." in reference to the last movie he saw "Dunston Checks in... to Club Med." Services will not be held as Garrett's animated corpse can be seen working almost every night.

author: Mike Eccher
title: Thanksgiving Day '95
bio: Mike Eccher is an enigma. No real bio is available at this time, just conjecture and speculation. What little has been gathered is that he grew up near Chicago, lives somewhere in Rochester, NY, attends a respectable Catholic college and, according to sources claiming to be neighbors, likes to monotonally scream Bruce Springstein lyrics in the shower with just a hint of irony. Rumors of him appearing in a Calvin Klein ad are still yet to be confirmed or dismissed.

bio: David Holzel is a writer and editor living somewhere near Washington, D.C. He studied mass communications at the University of Michigan, has lived in Jerusalem and Atlanta, was managing editor of Moment Magazine, and is looking forward to the millennium about as much as he's looking back to the last. His webzine, The Jewish Angle, tries hard to make sense of this zany world. https://davidwrotethis.wordpress.com

author: Marisa Brandt
title: Lost on 95
bio:
Marisa was born on Reagan's birthday, 1982. She first began reading to public audiences at the age of 15 and has been an active participant in the Rochester, NY spoken word scene ever since. Marisa also won first prize for poetry in the 1999 Sokol High School Literary Awards, sponsored by the Friends of the Rochester Public Library.

She is a pretty moody girl. She likes to draw comics, listen to "good" music, watch off-beat movies, pretend she can belly-dance and throw black olives at the cars that don't stop at the stopsign in front of her house. She reads an awful lot. She is very happy to have overcome a long bout of adolescence which has been plaguing her for several years.
